source.title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data
source.authors: Dominik Schnaus; Thomas Dagès; Daniel Cremers; Xi Wang; Phillip Isola

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It tests cross-modal shared geometry and the possibility of alignment using unpaired embeddings, but uses GeoWarP and alignment outcomes rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper's own experiments measure unpaired cross-modal alignment, geometry metrics, and how alignment varies with model, dataset, metric, and granularity. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter sweeps and comparisons that only evaluate GeoWarP's algorithmic components are omitted unless they also bear on a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper's own results bear on V4 (unpaired orthogonal mapping between independently trained models), V6 (how geometry metrics, granularity and subspace change measured agreement) and V7 (alignment is mostly coarse and absent for many pairs). It also gives a weak, hedged size observation for V1/V2. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. Independent models across many domains often share enough geometry for coarse unpaired cross-modal alignment, even across different datasets. Alignability is strongly predicted by CKA. Alignment is coarse rather than sample-exact and fails where geometry is not shared. A few pairs greatly improve it, and the result enables pair-free text-to-image generation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GeoWarP, a coarse CKA-based geometric initialization followed by Wasserstein Procrustes alignment, to test unpaired cross-modal correspondence. It does not directly reproduce a scale-and-capability convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies with model and dataset pairing, caption pooling, geometry metric, sample count, and granularity. In the reported metric comparisons, CKA predicts alignment more strongly than mutual k-NN, TSI, or QSI; the paper also reports sensitivity to PCA versus random subspaces and to clipping cosine similarities.

fits_no_version.finding: When one encoder embeds both modalities (MR/CT, RGB/thermal, SAR/optical, speakers), the identity map after centring already aligns them (FOSCTTM 0.000–0.177, Table 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A shared self-supervised encoder places different sensor modalities in an already-aligned space without fitting.

record.problems: The authors state that their experiment is not large enough to conclude whether larger models align better. Alignment is coarse and sometimes near chance or reversed; some geometry estimates use only a few hundred validation points and are acknowledged to have higher variance. Several granularity and clipping results are presented in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The individual cells for all vision-language model pairs across MS COCO, SPC, DCI, DOCCI, and the cross-dataset setting (Figs. 3, 9–13), and the full per-pair tables for NQ and NSD (Tables 8 and 10), were not individually extracted. The table-12 results include the failures and partial cases most relevant to V7; other detailed scientific-pair results are omitted for space. Component and hyperparameter ablations in Appendix A and additional generated-image scores in Tables 6–7 were omitted because they evaluate the proposed alignment system or downstream generation rather than the claim versions directly.

untested.parts: No controlled size or capability sweep, and no capability measure. Only an informal, hedged size remark.
No measure of model quality. Alignment is not related to vision or language model performance.
Entire version: no same-architecture, different-seed comparison.
Stitching layers and relative representations are not tested as mapping methods.
Entire version: no unit-, SAE-feature- or circuit-level comparison.
Not tested whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment. There is only an aside that Contriever, which was not trained on COCO, gives the same ordering in generation.

missing.what: MLIP↔MLIP (MP-20) FOSCTTM 0.00, CKA 0.89. Also SNARE-seq 0.21 with CKA 0.86 but mutual k-NN 0.04, and per-pair CKA/mutual k-NN/TSI values.
Few-pair results: zero-pair FOSCTTM and 79.6% CIFAR-10 top-1 for DINOv2-B/Qwen3; baselines need 100–500 pairs to match.

Generative token pooling fails on detailed captions (all methods near chance on SPC/DCI/DOCCI) and drops to chance zero-shot in the cross-dataset setting. ΔCKA flips sign with caption length (+0.099 COCO to −0.144 DOCCI).
Per-dataset vision-language FOSCTTM is markedly worse on DCI and DOCCI than on COCO, showing dependence on the input data.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'challenges' label on near-chance pairs was inverted: absent alignment supports V7 and challenges V4. The near-perfect NQ alignment is the actual V7 counterexample. r24–r26 were wrongly cited under V4. The single state per row is read against V4 for the V4/V7 rows; the problem text gives the V7 reading.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled scale sweep jointly varying model size and capability, or systematic capability measure; the paper notes its study is too small to conclude about model size.
Does not measure whether alignment increases as both vision and language models improve in performance.
Does not compare independently initialized networks of the same architecture for shared features or subspaces.
Tests learned orthogonal alignment from unpaired data, not stitching, relative representations as the main mapping, or alignment without paired data in general beyond its tested settings.
Does not test whether the same interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits recur across models.
Tests several geometry measures, datasets, and granularity choices, but not every reasonable metric, all settings of k, or a systematic out-of-distribution evaluation.
Shows incomplete and failed alignments, but does not causally test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality.
